title: Activate project card: receipts read plus one button that drives the chain
description:
SPIDR child C of task-bb844c288fb346c0856778c738b9f073. dependsOn child B (task-4b9c394debe94b41a80e2b46c6d55ab8). Filed by architect-d1711c47 2026-09-04, measured at main 68eb1c5d.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: (1) a daemon read that STATES each receipt as measured/missing with its reason, so the card can render before anything is clicked; (2) the v2 'Activate project' card that lists those receipts and drives register -> bind_repository -> provider.probe -> project.activate from one button.

MEASURED AT 68eb1c5d:
- COPY THIS PATTERN: apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/policy-install-port.ts (83 lines) already does exactly this shape for policy - `readSurfaceOnce` POSTs /affordances/read, `installStandardPolicy` loops the slices, RE-READS the surface between steps because each commit moves the aggregate version, finds the offer by commandKind, spends it via `spendOffer`, and STOPS AT THE FIRST REFUSAL keeping the daemon's own code+layer. Its consumer is apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/live-ops.tsx:95. Mirror it; do not invent a second dispatch idiom.
- The offer/refusal wire is apps/control-room/src/v2/approvals/offer-wire.ts (`spendOffer`, OfferOutcome) and apps/control-room/src/live/live-board-feed.ts (`frameOfSurface`, SurfaceFrame with .offers/.steps/.outcome/.connection).
- apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts is ALREADY 422 lines - over the 400 hard cap. DO NOT ADD TO IT. Add a separate route module alongside apps/daemon/src/http/policy-read.ts and runs-read.ts, which is the shipped idiom for a dedicated read.
- apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener.ts registers routes; a new read route is the 8-touchpoint + .js bridge pattern and needs its roster/roster-test backfill (bidirectional set-equality, global rail 9).
- The chain's four kinds and their prerequisite order are at apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts:31/:107; apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/work-labels.ts:46 already maps "project.activate" -> "Activate the project", so the card's labels come from there, not from new strings.

DESIGN (settled, do not re-derive): the card NEVER spells a witness - child B made the daemon mint it, so the card sends `project.activate` and shows the answer. Receipts render measured/missing with the DAEMON'S reason text verbatim, never a paraphrase, and never a credential value. The button drives the four commands SEQUENTIALLY, re-reading the surface between each (versions move), stopping at the first refusal with the daemon's code @ layer shown.

NOT IN SCOPE: the live-goal-create.ts copy replacement, the Playwright journey, README/runbook (all child D). Do not touch tests/e2e.
definitionOfDone: A dedicated daemon read module under apps/daemon/src/http/ (NOT affordance-read.ts, which is already 422 lines) answers with each of the six receipts as measured/missing plus its reason, sourced from child A's measurement surface; a test asserts a missing member is reported with its stable code and that no credential VALUE and no secret appears anywhere in the response body.

The route is registered in http-listener.ts and carries its .js bridge; the read-route roster and its asserting test are updated with BIDIRECTIONAL set-equality - enumerate the served set from the dispatch/route seam, not only from the roster constant (global rail 9), so deleting a route cannot stay green.

apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ gains an activation port mirroring policy-install-port.ts: it re-reads the surface between steps, finds each offer by commandKind, stops at the FIRST refusal, and keeps the daemon's own {code, layer}. Tests cover: all four commands accepted; a mid-chain refusal stopping the chain with the exact code; and an absent offer reported as its own code (not a guessed version).

The 'Activate project' card renders in the v2 project setup board, lists each receipt as measured/missing with its reason, and exposes one button driving register -> bind_repository -> provider.probe -> project.activate. Its testids are pinned in a control-room test (parent DoD 3).
signingKeyRef is displayed as NOT a trust boundary in v0.1 with its reason - never rendered as a measured receipt (human decision 2026-09-04).
The card shows refusals VERBATIM as the daemon's `code @ layer`; a test asserts a refusal is rendered unparaphrased.

Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. A bare `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for an apps/** claim - the root vitest include has no apps/** (global rail 18).
taskRails: MIRROR policy-install-port.ts; do not invent a second dispatch idiom. Re-read the surface between steps - each commit moves the aggregate version and a cached offer is a stale version.
DO NOT ADD LINES TO apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts (422 lines, over the 400 cap). A new read gets its own module beside policy-read.ts / runs-read.ts.
The card spells NO witness, NO version and NO payload the daemon can state itself. Refusals are shown as the daemon's own code @ layer, never rewritten, and no credential value may reach the DOM.

=== DECISION 1: THE READ MUST NOT WRITE (plan step-2's open question, resolved) ===
Child A's author's row is DONE, so I resolved it against the code rather than by asking. CONFIRMED WRITE PATH: `measureBackup` (-measure.ts:148-176) calls `ports.fs.mkdir(<root>/.moe-next/backups)` :157 then `ports.backup(storePath, destination)` :169, which in production is `copyStore` (-ports.ts:126) — a real node:sqlite ONLINE BACKUP writing a .sqlite file. Polled every 2 s by a card, that is a backup file per poll.
REJECTED: a "read-only backup probe" that digests the SOURCE in place and returns {ok:true, sha256}. An online sqlite backup checkpoints WAL, so the destination bytes do NOT digest to the source bytes; that ref would name a nonexistent file with a wrong digest = fabrication (epic rail 4).
CHOSEN: this route composes `nodeActivationReceiptPorts({ backup, fs })` with `fs.mkdir` a NO-OP (nothing is created on a read; every other fs member stays the real one, because measureStore/measureDistribution/credentialRef need real `exists`/`stat`/`readBytes`) and `backup` a refusing stub that never touches disk. The route then REPLACES the backup member row with its own honest arm: measured:false, code `ACTIVATION_READ_BACKUP_DEFERRED`, layer = this route's own LAYER, reason stating the backup is written by `project.activate` and never by a read. Belt-and-braces: even if child A's flow changes, the neutered ports cannot write. A test arm asserts `<root>/.moe-next` does NOT exist after a read.

=== DECISION 2: PRODUCTION COMPOSITION WIRING IS OUT OF THIS ROW ===

Wiring a real activation port also needs `StoreDependencyConfig` (:80) WIDENED with projectRoot / artifactRoot / agentCommand — it carries only projectId, storePath, nodeSpecsDir — plus every construction site. That is 4+ extra owned paths (breaching this row's 10 cap) and growth of a file already over cap. The approved plan names none of them. This row therefore lands the route registered and fail-closed with `LISTENER_ACTIVATION_UNAVAILABLE` when the port is absent — the shipped idiom every other read on this listener uses. Filing the gap as a row comment at step 6 with the exact symbols.

implementationPlan.description: THE READ MODULE. Create `apps/daemon/src/http/activation-read.ts` exporting `ACTIVATION_READ_PATH = "/activation/read"`, a LAYER const, a frozen `ACTIVATION_READ_CODES` array (capability denied / project mismatch / unreadable, mirroring POLICY_READ_CODES' three-code shape), the receipt view types, and the request handler. THIS ROUTE IS A READ: it measures and reports, and must NOT write the backup file or commit anything — if child A's measurement writes a backup as part of measuring, this route must call a read-only variant or the operator polls a card into writing a backup file every two seconds. Resolve that with child A's author and record the answer in a step note. Add the `.js` bridge sibling. Keep the module <=250 lines.

A foreign-project caller is refused BEFORE the body is read, so a malformed body cannot be used as an existence oracle.

=== THE READ-MUST-NOT-WRITE RESOLUTION, IMPLEMENTED ===
`readOnlyActivationPorts()` wraps `nodeActivationReceiptPorts(overrides)` and replaces exactly two members: `backup` becomes a stub returning `{ok:false, detail: ACTIVATION_READ_BACKUP_REASON}` WITHOUT opening a file, and `fs.mkdir` becomes `() => undefined`. `fs.exists`, `fs.stat` and `fs.readBytes` stay the REAL node implementations, because measureStore (-measure.ts:129,140), measureDistribution (:193-195) and credentialRef (:98) measure through them — neutering those would have silently degraded four members. `activationViewOf` then REPLACES the backup row outright with `deferredBackupRow()`: `measured:false`, `code: ACTIVATION_READ_BACKUP_DEFERRED`, `layer: LAYER` (this route's own — the ROUTE deferred it, child A's measurement did not fail), `reason: "not taken by a read: the store backup is written when project.activate runs"`. Nothing is fabricated: no ref, no digest, no file name for a file that does not exist.

`blocking` is DERIVED (unmeasured members minus the deferred backup), never spelled. Its JSDoc states the limit explicitly — an empty `blocking` means "nothing a read can see is blocking", NOT "activation will succeed" — so no boolean on this surface overclaims readiness the backup can still deny.

A measurement that THROWS is caught in `readActivation` and becomes `ACTIVATION_READ_UNREADABLE` at this layer, never a 500 with a stack trace (plan risk 5).

=== A REAL DEFECT THE STEP-4 SECRET ARM CAUGHT, AND THE FIX ===
The arm "leaks no credential value through a git STDERR tail either" FAILED on first run, verbatim:
`AssertionError: expected '{"blocking":["repository","distributi…' not to contain 'sk-ant-CANARY-…'`
with the wire payload carrying `"reason":"fatal: env ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=sk-ant-CANARY-3f9d2b7a1e4c6805-do-not-leak"` on BOTH the repository and distribution rows. Child A's `gitLine` (-measure.ts:62) passes a git stderr tail through `receiptDetail`, which only truncates to 600 chars and calls `toWellFormed()` — it does NOT redact. This route publishes that string straight onto an operator's screen and into e2e screenshots. This is plan risk 2 landing for real, not hypothetically.

FIXED AT THE BOUNDARY THAT PUBLISHES (this row's DoD sentence is about THIS response body): `activation-read.ts` now derives `secretValues(input, ports)` from the production `providerCredentials(providerFor(agentCommand), ports.env, exists)` — the SAME function the measurement uses — keeps entries with `secret === true` and a non-empty `value`, and `scrub()`s those values out of every row's `reason` and `ref` before they reach the wire, replacing them with `[redacted]`. Not a pattern guard (a `sk-` regex would be a negative-substring fence, not a fence); it redacts the exact values this daemon HOLDS. Where the agent command maps to no provider, no secret is held and nothing is redacted — honest, not silent.
NOT fixed upstream in `receiptDetail`: `activation-receipts-ports.ts` is child A's (DONE) and outside this row's owned paths. Recording it for the epic-final hardening row — the witness path in child B carries the same unredacted `detail` into `credentialRef`.
